title: Flatness of the constants map to a truncated power-series algebra
statement: For any commutative ring A and d,n ≥ 0, put B=A[[X_1,...,X_d]] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and I=ker(constantCoeff). The composite A -> B -> B/I^(n+1), given by constants and the quotient map, is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No local or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0EY9, first displayed calculation at a fixed index: finite monomial algebra calculation; coefficient criterion from Remark 032C.

proof.text: Use quotient_first_variables_kernels to identify I with the variables ideal. Specialize power_series_mem_combined_ideal_pow_iff to the zero base ideal. Its positive powers are zero, so membership in I^(n+1) is equivalent to vanishing of every coefficient of total degree below n+1.

The exponents E of total degree below n+1 form a finite type by Finsupp.finite_of_degree_lt. Define an A-linear map E -> A to B by summing the associated monomials, then compose with Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ. The surviving coefficients of that sum recover the input coordinates by coeff_monomial_same and coeff_monomial_ne.

Equality of quotient classes means the difference belongs to I^(n+1), hence all coordinate differences vanish: this proves injectivity. For surjectivity, take the surviving coefficients of any representative; subtracting their finite monomial sum leaves all these coefficients zero, hence an element of I^(n+1). LinearEquiv.ofBijective identifies the quotient with the finite free module E -> A. Apply Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv and RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff. The same formulas cover d=0, n=0, the zero ring and rings with nilpotents.

lean.statement:
theorem truncated_constants_flat (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (d n : ℕ) :
    ((Ideal.Quotient.mk
      ((RingHom.ker (constantCoeff (σ := Fin d) (R := A))) ^ (n + 1))).comp
        (C (σ := Fin d) (R := A))).Flat
